doc: The shape of the hierarchy changed through the designer's binding (hierarchical-requirement.fbl#markdown; FBL 0.7, sections 4.8, 5.5, 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4; DESL 0.2, section 5.3.5), on a document an agent wrote with LF endings and a title holding a character of two UTF-8 bytes, so that every offset after it is a byte offset and not a character offset. Its mark, line 2, names ITEM-0005 and REQ-0008, above the highest numbers in the file, ITEM-0004 and REQ-0007: REQ-0005, ITEM-0005 and REQ-0008 were given and deleted before. The steps build on each other: a requirement added below a selected one, numbered REQ-0009 from the mark, which shows that a deleted number is not given again; a sub-item added after an item's last child; an item with everything in it moved two columns deeper, with no number changed; a delete; and an add undone, with the mark restored. After the steps the document reads ITEM-0001 with REQ-0001, REQ-0002 and ITEM-0006, and ITEM-0004 with REQ-0007 and ITEM-0003, which holds REQ-0004, REQ-0009 and REQ-0006 with its description unchanged; the mark is ITEM-0006 REQ-0009. Every add is one edit of the new bullet and the mark line (FR-022, FR-025); none writes the registration. The first item of a file without the Requirements heading is no-section/ beside this one.

steps.doc: A requirement added below the selected REQ-0004, by addRequirementBelow: a create in its parent ITEM-0003 after it (User Story 4 scenario 3, FR-022). The add with position after is one insert-entry directly after that sibling's entry (FBL 6.4), at the end of the line span of REQ-0004, which runs to the end of its description's line (FBL 4.8, entries and spans; 6.3, where it goes). It takes the marker '*' and the column 2 of its previous sibling, REQ-0004 (6.3, a new item), with one space and the emit '{id} {title}'; the line ending is LF, the ending of the line its insertion point is on, not the binding's text.newline crlf, which serves a body without any ending (6.3, line endings). Its number: the mark on line 2 is REQ-0008 and the highest requirement number in the file REQ-0007, so the new id is one more than the higher, REQ-0009 (DESL 5.3.5); REQ-0008, which was given before and deleted, is not given again (FR-012). The mark is set to it in the same transaction, one replace-value of the group lastRequirement (FBL 6.3, lines: a changed value). One edit: the new bullet and the mark line (FR-025). The splices are listed with the mark's first: its id is made, and the mark set to it, when the transaction is first applied, before the element it is given to is created (DESL 5.3.1, 5.3.5), which is also the order of their offsets and the order the other fixtures of this designer list them in; FBL 6.4 orders an edit's splices as the transaction made its changes, and DESL 5.3.5 says only that both are in one transaction.

steps.doc: A sub-item added to ITEM-0001 by addItem, the control at the end of the item's content: a create with parent ITEM-0001 and no position, so the rule item's insert place last-child puts it after the last of the item's children, ITEM-0002 (FBL 6.2), after its line span, which ends with the line of REQ-0003 nested in it (FBL 4.8; 6.3, where it goes). It takes ITEM-0002's marker '-' and column 2 (6.3, a new item). Its number: the mark is ITEM-0005, the highest item number read ITEM-0004, so ITEM-0006, and the mark's group lastItem is replaced in the same edit, its splice listed first, as in the step before (DESL 5.3.5; FBL 6.3). Items and requirements are counted apart, so the requirement mark REQ-0009 stays (FR-010).
